personas.background: Marcus moved to the area three years ago for work and joined the cycling club looking for weekend company. Self-taught mechanic; can fix a derailleur faster than anyone in the group. Tends to plan routes obsessively and gets mildly irritated when people suggest shortcuts.

food.value: prefers a proper cooked breakfast after long rides — never touches the pastries the others bring

activities.value: favours hill climbs over flat loops — always pushes for routes with 400m+ elevation

social.value: dislikes last-minute route changes; prefers routes finalised at least two days before the ride

domain_specific.value: rides a carbon road bike; subtly dismissive of e-bikes in the group

preference_history.old_value: insists on 80km+ every weekend — turns down anything shorter as 'not worth it'
preference_history.new_value: accepts 50-60km rides after a knee injury forced him to reconsider; grudgingly admits they can still be challenging
preference_history.trigger: physio told him to reduce load for six weeks after a training overuse injury

speaking_quirks: opens messages with 'Right —' when moving to logistics
uses 'noted' as a single-word acknowledgement
rarely uses punctuation mid-message but always ends with a full stop

personas.background: Priya joined the club after a friend recommended it as a way to decompress from screen-heavy work. She's one of the faster climbers in the group despite only cycling seriously for two years. Has a habit of suggesting post-ride coffee spots and is the de-facto social organiser.

food.value: always finds a café with oat milk — quietly judges places that don't stock it

activities.value: prefers routes that end somewhere picturesque — route aesthetics matter as much as distance to her

social.value: enjoys longer coffee stops; gets restless when the group rushes back immediately after rides

domain_specific.value: rides a gravel bike; enthusiastic about mixed-surface routes the roadies in the group avoid

preference_history.old_value: sticks strictly to tarmac — nervous about off-road handling
preference_history.new_value: actively seeks gravel sections after investing in a new bike and discovering she loves the variety
preference_history.trigger: bought a gravel bike and did her first off-road loop with Tomás

preference_history.old_value: happy with fortnightly group rides — uses solo rides to fill the gaps
preference_history.new_value: pushes for weekly group rides after realising the social side motivates her training more than solo miles
preference_history.trigger: had a string of unmotivated solo sessions; Marcus jokingly pointed out she only hits PBs with the group

speaking_quirks: uses strings of emojis to punctuate excitement 🚴🔥
starts planning messages with 'ok ok ok so —'
refers to coffee stops as 'the actual reason we ride'

personas.background: Tomás has been cycling since his twenties and is the informal elder statesman of the group. He brought most of the current members in by word of mouth. Calm under pressure, excellent at reading weather, and never forgets to check if newcomers are comfortable with the pace.

food.value: always brings his own energy bars — rarely buys from cafés; doesn't like the sugar crash from shop pastries

activities.value: prefers a moderate 70km tempo ride over extreme distances; thinks the group does too many sufferfest routes

social.value: values punctuality at start points — quietly annoyed when people arrive late and delay the group

domain_specific.value: prefers riding at the back to keep an eye on slower members rather than chasing the front group

preference_history.old_value: 8am Saturday starts — rigid about early mornings for cooler temperatures and lighter traffic
preference_history.new_value: willing to push to 9am after repeatedly losing members who couldn't manage early alarms; prioritises group size over timing
preference_history.trigger: two members dropped out of consecutive sessions citing the early start; Tomás polled the group and shifted the time

speaking_quirks: ends practical messages with 'sorted' or 'all good'
uses 'lads' as a gender-neutral address for the whole group
almost never uses exclamation marks — flatness is his default tone

personas.background: Yuki took up cycling during the pandemic as a mental health strategy and never stopped. She's still building fitness but makes up for it with enthusiasm and a willingness to try any route. Works long hours and sometimes has to drop out of rides at short notice due to work deadlines.

food.value: brings rice balls for long rides — always offers them around and is visibly pleased when people try one

activities.value: prefers flatter recovery rides after a heavy work week — avoids the brutal climb routes when she's sleep-deprived

social.value: more comfortable in the smaller sub-groups that form on long climbs than in the full-group café stop

domain_specific.value: obsessively tracks Strava metrics but gets anxious when others compare times out loud

preference_history.old_value: hangs back with the slower tail — avoids being dropped and finds it embarrassing
preference_history.new_value: starts pushing into the middle group after consistent training gains; occasionally sits at the front on flat sections
preference_history.trigger: completed a structured six-week training block and noticed the middle group no longer dropped her on hills

speaking_quirks: uses '!!' instead of full sentences when excited
often replies with a single word or very short phrase, then follows up with a longer message
typos in almost every message but never corrects them

personas.background: Derek retired early and joined the club looking for structure after leaving work. He's methodical and likes having a training plan even for recreational rides. Owns more cycling gear than anyone else in the group. His adult son also cycles but rides with a different club.

food.value: brings a protein shake in a branded shaker — dismissive of the post-ride café culture the younger members love

activities.value: prefers regimented, reproducible routes — dislikes spontaneous diversions mid-ride

social.value: prefers to cycle home straight after rides rather than socialise — occasionally makes exceptions for a quick coffee

domain_specific.value: advocates loudly for hi-viz gear and helmet cameras; slightly preachy about road safety

preference_history.old_value: always leaves immediately after rides — considers socialising a waste of recovery time
preference_history.new_value: started staying for coffee roughly half the time after his wife encouraged him to invest more in friendships
preference_history.trigger: his wife pointed out he'd been isolated since retiring; he quietly started staying on

speaking_quirks: writes full sentences with correct punctuation even in casual chat
prefixes suggestions with 'For reference —' or 'For what it's worth —'
never uses contractions in writing

personas.background: Saoirse grew up in a cycling family and is comfortably the most technically skilled rider in the group. She can be quietly competitive but keeps it mostly contained. Splits her time between the group and a women's racing league on weekday evenings. Often brings design sensibility to kit discussions.

food.value: partial to a post-ride pizza — was the one who established the informal pizza tradition for big milestone rides

activities.value: loves technical descents; always volunteers to lead the group down unfamiliar hills

social.value: prefers smaller group rides for quality conversation — finds full nine-person rides unwieldy

domain_specific.value: opinionated about kit aesthetics — the group quietly defers to her on jersey design choices

preference_history.old_value: treats group rides as a secondary option — often skips for racing league events
preference_history.new_value: prioritises the group ride most weekends after the racing league restructured its fixture schedule
preference_history.trigger: her racing league moved its events to Saturday evenings, freeing up Saturday mornings

preference_history.old_value: pushes for race-pace intervals on group rides — expects others to keep up
preference_history.new_value: dials back the race mentality on group rides after Tomás pointed out she was demoralising newer riders
preference_history.trigger: Tomás had a quiet word after Yuki mentioned feeling left behind two sessions running

speaking_quirks: uses sarcasm dryly and without emoji — can read as blunt until you know her
references racing terms casually ('tempo', 'breakaway', 'sitting in') in non-racing contexts
signs off long messages with a dash and no name

personas.background: Ben cycles as a counterpoint to long shifts and unpredictable on-call hours. He's known for missing rides with no warning when he gets called in, which the group has learned to accept with varying degrees of grace. Easy-going, widely liked, brings a relaxed energy that offsets some of the group's more intense personalities.

food.value: always orders a flat white and something savoury — never touches anything with icing

activities.value: prefers shorter weekday rides when he can manage them over the big weekend epics — easier to fit into on-call life

social.value: thrives in the café stop banter; often the one who keeps the group at the table longest

domain_specific.value: quietly sceptical of extreme training plans; often plays down injuries in the group chat and underplays fatigue

preference_history.old_value: completely passive on planning — shows up or doesn't, never weighs in on route decisions
preference_history.new_value: started suggesting routes occasionally after Marcus called him out for contributing zero opinions over a whole season
preference_history.trigger: Marcus made a pointed joke in the chat about Ben's consistent vote-abstaining

speaking_quirks: uses 'haha' frequently even when only mildly amused
tends to follow apologetic messages with 'next one, promise'
often abbreviates to single letters: 'k', 'y', 'np'

personas.background: Lena joined the club through a patient who kept talking about it in sessions. She's the group's unofficial injury consultant and is called on constantly for advice on aches and saddle fit. Thoughtful, measured in her opinions, and the one most likely to ask how someone is actually feeling rather than just giving a thumbs-up.

food.value: eats a proper meal before rides rather than during — nurses a tea rather than ordering food at café stops

activities.value: prefers consistent moderate rides over sporadic big efforts — talks openly about injury prevention periodisation

social.value: one-to-one conversations alongside a ride feel more natural to her than group chat banter

domain_specific.value: the group's go-to for saddle height, cleat angle, and knee pain — sometimes resents how much informal consulting happens on rides

preference_history.old_value: avoids gradients above 8% — cautious after a hip flexor issue the previous year
preference_history.new_value: comfortably takes on 10-12% gradients after six months of targeted rehab work on her own hip
preference_history.trigger: completed her own rehabilitation programme and tested it on the Cranfield ridge route

speaking_quirks: often writes in full paragraphs even for simple chat messages
qualifies opinions with 'from a physio perspective' or 'clinically speaking'
sends voice notes when the message is too long — but always follows up with a text summary

personas.background: Callum found the group through Strava after following Priya's activity log. He's the newest member and still finding his place socially, though he's quickly established himself as the fastest on flat segments. Tends to over-rely on tech — GPS, heart-rate monitors, power meters — and can get defensive when people question his gadget-heavy approach.

food.value: eats during rides via precisely portioned gels — finds the café stop inefficient and occasionally skips it

activities.value: gravitates towards flat, fast circuits where power output is measurable — indifferent to scenic routes

social.value: more engaged in the group on digital channels than in person — responds quickly in the chat but quiet at café stops

domain_specific.value: builds and shares custom Strava dashboards for the group; proud of this but slightly wounded when people don't engage with them

preference_history.old_value: treats the group as a training vehicle — civil but detached, rarely engages in non-cycling chat
preference_history.new_value: starts joining the post-ride café stop more reliably after Priya explicitly invited him in and the banter won him over
preference_history.trigger: Priya told him directly that half the group thought he didn't like them; he was surprised and made a visible effort

speaking_quirks: links to Strava or Garmin data in place of describing a ride in words
uses precise numbers where others would round ('47.3 km' not '~50 km')
never uses punctuation beyond full stops

edges.history_summary: Marcus and Tomás set up the WhatsApp group together after meeting at a local sportive two years ago. They disagree regularly on route design but trust each other completely on safety decisions.
shared_events: founded the club together after the Ashdown Sportive
planned and led the club's first multi-day trip to the Cotswolds

edges.history_summary: Marcus and Priya get on well despite different cycling philosophies — she adds the social glue he lacks, and he provides the route rigour she'd never plan herself.
shared_events: shared a puncture repair in the rain on the first long club ride
argued amicably over café vs. home lunch for the midsummer ride

edges.history_summary: Marcus and Derek bond over their shared preference for discipline and proper preparation. Both get quietly frustrated by last-minute changes, which creates an occasional alliance against the group's more spontaneous members.
shared_events: both complained about the same last-minute route change in session 4
completed a solo century ride together before Derek's knee started playing up

edges.history_summary: Tomás recruited Priya into the club through a mutual friend. He treats her as one of the group's social cornerstones and she genuinely looks up to his experience.
shared_events: first off-road loop together that converted Priya to gravel riding
organised the surprise birthday ride for Marcus together

edges.history_summary: Priya noticed Callum's Strava segments overlapping with club routes and directly messaged him to join. She's invested in making sure he integrates well and occasionally feels responsible for his social awkwardness.
shared_events: first ride Callum did with the group — Priya paced him at the back
Priya intervened when the group complained about Callum's data-dump messages

edges.history_summary: Tomás was patient with Yuki when she was clearly struggling with the pace in early sessions. She's grateful; he's pleased by her improvement. A quiet mutual respect.
shared_events: Tomás dropped back to ride with Yuki for 20km when she struggled on the ridge loop
celebrated Yuki's first sub-3hr century ride with the group

edges.history_summary: Tomás and Saoirse have cycled together for years through overlapping club memberships. They share a mutual respect that comes from years of riding in all conditions together.
shared_events: rode the same club sportive three years before founding Cranfield CC
only two members who've done the full Cranfield Ridge 100km loop unsupported

edges.history_summary: Ben and Tomás clicked immediately — Tomás appreciates Ben's ease under pressure and Ben appreciates Tomás's non-judgmental reaction when he has to bail on rides at short notice.
shared_events: Ben provided on-the-spot medical advice when Tomás took a minor fall on a wet descent
shared a long solo training week before the club was formed

edges.history_summary: Yuki briefly saw Lena professionally for a knee complaint before realising she was in the same cycling club. The professional relationship has faded but left a residual dynamic where Yuki defers to Lena on physical matters.
shared_events: first ride after Yuki's knee clearance — Lena monitored her pace
both missed the Ashdown ride and went on a shorter two-person loop instead

edges.history_summary: Derek and Lena have never fully clicked. Derek finds Lena's clinical approach to rides slightly condescending; Lena finds Derek's bluntness occasionally unkind to newer members. They're polite but keep their distance.
shared_events: clashed indirectly when Derek made a dismissive comment about Yuki's pace and Lena called it out in the chat
reluctantly co-led a session when Tomás was away

edges.history_summary: Saoirse and Ben maintain an easy, low-key friendship built on mutual teasing. She mocks his last-minute cancellations; he deflects with self-deprecating humour. Neither takes it seriously.
shared_events: first ones to arrive and last to leave at the club's winter social
jointly refused to do the sub-zero January ride and organised a café ride instead

edges.history_summary: Saoirse and Callum are the two fastest in the group on different terrain — she on climbs and descents, he on flat power. There's an unspoken competitiveness that occasionally surfaces as pointed comments in the chat.
shared_events: matched each other on the final flat stretch of a club ride, neither willing to concede a sprint
exchanged clipped comments about route choice when neither agreed with Marcus's selection

edges.history_summary: Ben and Lena share a healthcare background and often compare notes on overtraining and recovery. They sometimes form a quiet consensus on injury-related group decisions that the others tend to accept.
shared_events: jointly advised Marcus when he mentioned knee pain in the chat
co-wrote the group's informal 'when to rest' guidance after too many members pushing through niggles

edges.history_summary: Marcus and Saoirse respect each other's technical competence but clash on route philosophy — Marcus wants elevation, Saoirse wants technical descents. They've had a few public disagreements in the group chat.
shared_events: argued over the route for the club's anniversary ride in a thread the whole group watched
made up by co-designing a route that satisfied both: steep climb, technical descent

edges.history_summary: Priya and Yuki bond over being the younger women in the group. Priya often checks in on Yuki after tough rides and Yuki shares Strava analytics with Priya who actually looks at them.
shared_events: shared a flat tyre repair during the first gravel loop
started a side thread to plan a women's cycling weekend that the group doesn't know about yet

group_norms.norm_text: we always stop for coffee after rides, no exceptions
everyone shares their Strava after every ride
no one gets left behind — we regroup at every summit
we vote on route options before every Saturday ride
the club buys pizza for anyone who completes their first 100km ride
